name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Huge Democratic fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean plus a favorable environment points to a comfortable Democratic margin, and Hamawy has out-raised Mele by roughly 19-to-1 with substantial outside support while Mele has almost no cash. Markets price a Democratic win near 96%, consistent with a Safe D call despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unusually strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Bonnie Watson Coleman is retiring, leaving an open seat in a central New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about 13 points. Democrat Adam Hamawy has raised over $1.5 million and benefits from nearly $2 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars on hand. No independent groups are opposing the Democrat.

With no public polls and no expert ratings, the outlook rests on fundamentals, and those point clearly Democratic: the district lean, a favorable national environment, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 96% chance. An open seat adds some uncertainty, but the seat remains safely in Democratic hands.
